intended_object: Semilocal simple connectivity at a point x: x has a neighbourhood U such that every loop in U based at x is null-homotopic in X, i.e. π₁(U,x) → π₁(X,x) is trivial (Brazas, Def. 2.1; the based version of Hatcher's notion). Taken from the docstring.
explanation: The definition asks for some U ∈ 𝓝 x such that every loop `γ : Path x x` whose image lies in U satisfies `γ.Homotopic (Path.refl x)`. `Path.Homotopic` is homotopy relative to the endpoints, taken in X. That is the same as saying the map π₁(U,x) → π₁(X,x) induced by inclusion is trivial. The definition takes U to be any neighbourhood rather than an open set, and the two versions are equivalent: if U works, its interior also works, because a loop in the interior is a loop in U, and any open neighbourhood is in particular a neighbourhood. The setting is arbitrary topological spaces, which is the natural generality. A search of Mathlib for "semilocally" turned up only a docstring mention of "semilocally contractible" in `Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/LocallyContractible.lean`, so Mathlib has no counterpart definition.
